facts.fact: IPI states Mali amended its Penal Code in December 2024, incorporating provisions previously contained in the 2019 cybercrime law, and that journalists have been arrested and imprisoned under the new penal code.
facts.system: Penal Code cybercrime provisions (ex-2019 cybercrime law)

facts.fact: IPI reports that journalist Chahana Takiou, editor of 22 Septembre, was arrested in June 2026 by the National Cybercrime Unit and sentenced on 3 August 2026 to 12 months with six suspended, and fined, for undermining the credibility of the state.
facts.system: Penal Code cybercrime provisions (ex-2019 cybercrime law)

facts.fact: IPI reports journalist Abdrahamane Keita of Le Témoin was detained on 9 June 2026 and charged with undermining national unity and the credibility of the state and spreading false information; his trial was postponed from 17 to 31 August.
facts.system: Penal Code cybercrime provisions (ex-2019 cybercrime law)

facts.fact: IPI reports that the trial of commentator Mohamed Youssouf Bathily (Ras Bath) began on 10 August 2026 on charges of criminal association and undermining the credibility of the state through information and communication technologies.
facts.system: Penal Code cybercrime provisions (ex-2019 cybercrime law)
